whatItDoes: Post a message to Slack using your own bot token. The starter for calling any outside service with your own credential — fork it, repoint the endpoint and the credential, and it notifies Discord, PagerDuty, or your own webhook instead.
longDescription:
Post a message to Slack using your own bot token, which Sapiom collects when you use this template and hands to the run as an environment variable. Slack is the hook, but the real lesson is transferable: store a secret, read it at runtime, call an API. Swap Slack for anything else by changing the `fetch` URL and the credential key.

It runs two steps. `validate` checks the message and settles the config — which credential to use and, for bot mode, which channel. `post` reads the token from the environment Sapiom injected it into and calls Slack directly: either `chat.postMessage` with a bot token, which returns the channel and message timestamp, or an incoming-webhook URL, where the channel is fixed by the URL. The token is never written into the code.

You can trace the whole thing before you have a token. `run_local` runs in dryRun mode, and a missing credential behaves the same way — the graph runs validate → post end to end and returns `posted: false` with `skipped` telling you why, without touching the network.

Nothing here calls a paid model. It calls no metered capability at all: the Slack request goes out on your own token, so a run costs you nothing on Sapiom.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

This one needs a secret before it can post for real. It runs with no setup: with no credential set it composes the message, reports `posted: false, skipped: "no-credential"`, and says what it would have sent. To post for real, supply `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` (a bot token with `chat:write`) and a `channel`, or `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` for webhook mode — Sapiom asks for these when you use the template. Until you set it, runs trace the full graph and return `posted: false, skipped: "no-credential"` instead of failing. For bot mode, also pass a `channel` (like `#general`); webhook mode carries the channel in the URL. To point this at another service, change the `fetch` URL and the credential key in `index.ts` and store that API's key under the matching ref.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` to trace the whole flow with no Sapiom capability spend (it skips the network), or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.

requiredSecrets.label: Slack bot token
requiredSecrets.description: A Slack bot token (`xoxb-…`) with `chat:write`. Without it the run composes the message and posts nothing.

requiredSecrets.label: Slack incoming-webhook URL
requiredSecrets.description: Only for `via: "webhook"`. The channel is baked into the URL.

settings.label: Slack channel
settings.description: Channel name or id for bot mode. Ignored by webhook mode, where the URL carries it.
